title: Rennes vs PSG: Duelo que abre a Ligue 1 2026-2027
seoTitle: Rennes vs PSG: Opener for Ligue 1 2026-2027
subtitle: Parisian side seeks sextuple while Breton side looks to surprise
excerpt: On Sunday, August 23, 2026, Roazhon Park hosts PSG in the match opening the first round of Ligue 1.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The clash between Rennes and PSG marks the opening of Ligue 1 2026-2027, with kickoff on Sunday, August 23, 2026, at 3:45 PM (Brasilia time), at Roazhon Park in Rennes. The Parisian side, five-time consecutive champions and two-time Champions League winners, was supposed to debut at the Parc des Princes, but a fungus that destroyed the pitch after a heatwave forced the league to swap the home venue.

PSG arrives as favorite carrying the weight of recent titles

PSG appears as the clear favorite in consulted projections, with an estimated probability of victory for the Parisians above 70%. The team arrives at the first round carrying the weight of a nearly perfect 2025/2026 season: Ligue 1 title with 76 points, second consecutive Champions League, and the UEFA Super Cup won against Aston Villa in August. The 1-0 defeat to Lens in the Trophée des Champions, however, showed that Luis Enrique's team is still seeking fine-tuning for the new season.

Squad changes that alter the dynamic

The transfer market significantly altered the squad: Gonçalo Ramos left for Milan for 75 million euros, Kang-In Lee left the club, and Randal Kolo Muani moved to Juventus. To replace them, Maghnes Akliouche (Monaco), Ferran Torres (Barcelona), Lucas Digne (Aston Villa), and young Mika Godts (Ajax) arrived. Bradley Barcola, not even called up for the Trophée des Champions, is heading for a transfer to Liverpool.

Rennes prepares to challenge the giant

Rennes finished the 2025-2026 season in sixth place, with 59 points, securing a spot in the Europa League. The arrival of Franck Haise in February 2026 transformed the team: eight wins in the last 12 league games and only three defeats under the former Lens coach. The Breton club invested in the market with the signing of Eliezer Mayenda (Sunderland, 22 million euros) and the loan of defender Charlie Cresswell (Toulouse), as well as Issa Soumaré, who arrived on a free transfer from Le Havre. The squad became shorter with the departure of Jérémy Jacquet and the loan of Jordan James to Wolverhampton, which could weigh on a calendar that includes Ligue 1 and Europa League.

Head-to-head history and match expectations

In 50 confrontations since 2003, PSG sums 26 wins against 15 for Rennes and nine draws, with 84 goals scored by the Parisians and 45 by the Bretons. The 2025-2026 season produced two opposite results: on December 6, 2025, PSG thrashed them 5-0 at the Parc des Princes, with Kvaratskhelia and Senny Mayulu leading the performance. In the return match, on February 13, 2026, Rennes replied with a 3-1 win at Roazhon Park, with goals from Mussa Al-Taamari, Esteban Lepaul, and Breel Embolo. If they win this Sunday, Rennes will secure two consecutive wins over PSG in Ligue 1, something that hasn't happened in three years.

Confirmed lineups and critical points

Confirmed Rennes lineup (4-3-3): Brice Samba; Mahamadou Nagida, Charlie Cresswell, Abdelhamid Aït Boudlal, and Przemyslaw Frankowski; Valentin Rongier, Adrien Thomasson, and Sebastian Szymanski; Soumaré, Esteban Lepaul, and Tamari. Coach: Franck Haise. The future of Breel Embolo remains undefined: the Swiss forward receives inquiries from English clubs and may leave Rennes before the window closes. Nuno Mendes is suspended after a red card in the Trophée des Champions against Lens, opening space for Lucas Digne at left back. Maghnes Akliouche is available and could integrate the starting group or be an option on the bench for the first game of the season. Lucas Chevalier, already at the club since last season, remains on the bench, with Matvey Safonov keeping the starting position. Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye, both in exit negotiations, should not be listed. Ferran Torres, signed from Barcelona, seeks to make his official debut with the Parisian shirt. Confirmed PSG lineup (4-3-3): Matvey Safonov; Achraf Hakimi, Marquinhos, Willian Pacho, and Lucas Hernandez; Zaïre-Emery, Vitinha, and Neves; Désiré Doué, Ousmane Dembélé, and Kvaratskhelia. Coach: Luis Enrique. PSG should line up in the usual 4-3-3, with Vitinha and Zaïre-Emery in midfield and Dro Fernandez in a more advanced role, while Digne replaces Nuno Mendes with a more defensive profile at left back. Rennes' fragility may lie in defense: with Cresswell adapting and Camara absent in midfield, defensive coverage against the incursions of Kvaratskhelia and Dembélé will be the most sensitive point for the Bretons. Although the exact score is a higher-risk market, analysis of recent data supports the expectation of an open game, with PSG coming out on top after 90 minutes.
